A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEFLECT study. Their main text, equations, Figures 1–4, Tables 1–8 and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and segmentation experiments across five datasets and three geospatial foundation models, plus ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results in Table 2, ablations in Tables 3–6, and initialization and displacement analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same untangled patch embedding, untangled attention and norm-constrained embedding deflection procedure, including optional low-rank parameterization. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate classification on So2Sat, Brick Kiln and ForestNet, and segmentation on MADOS and BurnScars. Section 5.1 and Appendix A retain the same data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains frozen and full-finetuning baselines, Norm Tuning, BitFit, LoRA and SLR. Table 4 retains the LoRA comparison, and Tables 7–8 retain the same finetuning, frozen, BitFit and SLR initialization comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings remain identical: classification uses 60 epochs and batch size 24; segmentation uses 120 epochs and batch size 8. Input resizing, prediction heads, metrics, model configurations, data splits and ablation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices B–C retain the same analyses of adapted layers, low-rank dimensions, feature projection, pixel sampling, displacement norms and weight initialization. Tables 3–8 and Figure 4 add or remove no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 4's standard deviation across pretrained models. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings in Tables 2–8 and Figures 1 and 4 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains DEFLECT MADOS mIoU values of 50.6, 51.6 and 38.2 for Scale-MAE, DINO-MC and Cross-Scale MAE, respectively.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same embedding-decomposition assumption, attention derivations and constrained optimization formulation in Equations 1–12. No mathematical definition, argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and parameter-efficiency claims, including adaptation from RGB to multispectral imagery and competitive accuracy with 5–10 times fewer parameters. The publication header adds no scientific claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of spectral redundancy, performance stability, layer selection, displacement norms and initialization sensitivity remain unchanged. Section 6 also retains the same proposed extensions to hyperspectral, temporal, SAR and depth inputs.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same preprocessing, feature statistics, adapted layers, rank, initialization and optimizer details. Both versions promise future code release without adding access instructions or a code link.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 2's positioning relative to geospatial foundation models and parameter-efficient adaptation are unchanged. The ICCV publication notice does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'Published as a conference paper at ICCV 2025' and updates the arXiv version/date line. The body wording, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page gains a publication banner and horizontal rule, with small spacing and line-wrap differences elsewhere. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–8 retain their content, designs and placement.

improvement.justification: The method, experimental evidence, mathematical reasoning and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices. The publication notice and minor typesetting differences do not materially improve or diminish the paper's clarity, rigor or overall quality.
